file_layer.location: no production path exists; adapter is path-agnostic. Test target = std::filesystem::temp_directory_path()/'verdigris-task-0030.snapshot' (native/tests/core_tests.cpp:857-858)
file_layer.atomic_write: temp file '<target>.tmp' written+flushed, then MoveFileExW(MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING|MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH) on Windows / std::filesystem::rename elsewhere; failure removes the temp file and throws filesystem_error
file_layer.read: whole-file slurp; open/size/read failures throw runtime_error
known_gaps: ofstream::flush() reaches the OS, not the platter: no fsync/FlushFileBuffers on the temp file before rename; MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH covers rename metadata, not prior data blocks
no directory fsync after POSIX rename: crash can lose the rename even though the temp data landed
fixed '.tmp' suffix: two concurrent writers to one target collide on the same temp path; no unique-temp or lock protocol; no startup sweep of orphaned .tmp files
Windows replace fails when a reader holds the target open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE (sharing violation); no retry/backoff around read-vs-replace races
v1 bytes carry no checksum/trailer: same-length corruption inside a hex string or decimal number decodes silently into different values

negative_control.claim: one realistic partial-write/stale-version case not covered by any current test
negative_control.case: TORN OR MANGLED SAVE: a cloud-sync client (OneDrive/Dropbox) or antivirus truncates/mangles the House file between sessions. write_atomic guarantees the target is never torn by OUR writer, but external mutation produces either (a) a truncated byte stream or (b) a same-length flip inside a hex string/decimal number. Case (a) must fail restore with 'missing snapshot field'; case (b) SILENTLY restores divergent state because v1 carries no digest. Neither behavior is asserted by any test today.
negative_control.secondary_case: STALE VERSION: restore(bytes starting schemaVersion=2) must throw; implemented at native/src/core.cpp:1230-1233 but zero tests exercise the rejection branch.
